topic: How does GPS know where you are?
research_summary: Candidates: (1) How does GPS know where you are? 35/40 (everyday, huge curiosity gap, clean visual mechanism, not yet covered), (2) Why does a phone get warm while charging? 31, (3) How does a QR code store data? 30. Winner: GPS; sat in the 'How Tech Works' niche that the channel has barely used, and the follow-up 'Google Maps traffic' continues the cluster. Titles considered (/50): 'How Does GPS Know Where You Are? (Your Phone Never Calls)' 43 (chosen); 'Your Phone Never Calls Anyone, Yet It Finds You' 41; 'GPS Is Just A Stopwatch' 39; 'How Satellites Find You In 0.07 Seconds' 38; 'What Your Phone Hears From Space' 37; 'GPS Without Internet?' 36; 'The Clock That Finds You' 35; 'How GPS Really Works' 33; 'Why GPS Needs Four Satellites' 34; 'The Maths Behind The Blue Dot' 37. Thumbnails: A a phone with a glowing dot and three circles crossing (chosen, 'YOUR PHONE ONLY LISTENS'), B a satellite shouting at a tiny phone, C a stopwatch over a map pin. Hooks: 'Your phone knows exactly where you are, and it never says a word' (chosen); 'Your phone never calls a satellite, yet it finds you'; 'A stopwatch finds you anywhere on Earth'; 'GPS satellites do not know you exist'; 'You are being located by a clock'. FACTS (status): GPS satellites orbit in medium Earth orbit at about 20,200 km and circle twice a day - VERIFIED (gps.gov Space Segment); about thirty operational satellites (31 on the gps.gov page, stated as 'about thirty') - VERIFIED; a receiver needs at least four satellites for a fix: three for position and one to solve its own clock error - VERIFIED (standard GPS description, gps.gov / NASA); the phone only receives and never transmits to the satellites - VERIFIED (GPS is a passive one-way system). Signal travel time about 0.067 s = 20,200 km / 299,792 km/s, own arithmetic for a satellite straight overhead - COMPUTED, labelled as computed on screen. The 2D circle picture is a simplification of 3D trilateration with spheres - PARTIALLY VERIFIED, said as 'circles'. Sources: https://archive.gps.gov/systems/gps/space/ , https://www.nasa.gov/directorates/somd/space-communications-navigation-program/gps/ . scenes.text: Your phone knows exactly where you are, and it never says a word.
Weird, right? So how does it know? Let's ask.
About thirty satellites circle twenty thousand kilometres up. Each keeps shouting its clock time. Your phone just listens.
Here's the trick. Light is fast, but not instant. A late signal means a far satellite.
Guess how long the signal takes from space? About sixty-seven milliseconds. Faster than a blink.
One distance puts you on a circle. A second narrows it down. A third crosses at a single point. That's you.
Quick quiz: how many satellites does your phone really need? Three for position, plus one to fix its clock.
So GPS is a stopwatch and some geometry. Which app do you use GPS in the most? Tell me below!

scenes.text: आपका फ़ोन जानता है आप कहाँ हैं, और वो एक शब्द भी नहीं बोलता।
अजीब है ना? तो पता कैसे चलता है?
लगभग तीस सैटेलाइट घूमते हैं, हर एक अपनी घड़ी का समय बताता है। फ़ोन बस सुनता है।
असली चाल: रोशनी तेज़ है, पर तुरंत नहीं पहुँचती। देर से आया सिग्नल, यानी दूर सैटेलाइट।
अंदाज़ा लगाइए, सिग्नल कितनी देर में आता है? लगभग सड़सठ मिलीसेकंड, पलक झपकने से भी तेज़।
एक दूरी आपको एक घेरे पर रखती है। तीन घेरे एक बिंदु पर मिलते हैं। वही आप हैं।
छोटा क्विज़: फ़ोन को कितने सैटेलाइट चाहिए? तीन जगह के लिए, एक घड़ी के लिए।
तो GPS स्टॉपवॉच और ज्यामिति है। आप इसे किस ऐप में सबसे ज़्यादा चलाते हैं? कमेंट में बताइए!
